Hey there—great effort stepping into Warrior One! I love the focus and intention you’re bringing to the pose. Let’s fine-tune a few key alignment points so you can build strength, stability, and ease in the posture. I’ll speak directly to what you’ve shared, and I promise—these are very common, totally adjustable details!

First, **your spine isn’t quite straight**—I notice a little rounding or compression through the lower back. To support a long, neutral spine, gently draw your tailbone down (like tucking it slightly under) and lift the crown of your head toward the ceiling. Imagine a string gently pulling you upward from the top of your head—this helps lengthen the whole back body without overarching or collapsing.

Second, **your arms aren’t fully extending straight up**—they’re slightly angled forward or bent at the elbows. Try reaching your fingertips *actively* toward the sky—not just lifting your arms, but *growing* them long from your shoulders. Keep your shoulders relaxed away from your ears, and palms facing each other (or thumbs forward) to help keep the arms aligned with your ears and your chest open.

Third, **your front knee isn’t positioned directly over your ankle**—it’s drifting slightly forward past the toes or collapsing inward. To correct this, make sure your front knee tracks straight over your second and third toes—not beyond them, and not collapsing in. A helpful cue: press firmly through the outer edge of your back foot while engaging your inner thigh muscles—this brings stability and helps align the knee with the ankle naturally.

You’re doing beautifully—these small refinements will make a big difference in how grounded, strong, and energized you feel in the pose. Let’s take a breath together, reset, and try it again—slowly, mindfully. You’ve got this! 🌟
